en.html:
The rear approach went round in a spiral, deeper underground.

Width was not generous. Height also, nothing to boast of. The Grand Commander and his horse, Muramasa and myself pretending to be priests—only these were moving. But the noise! In that narrow space, every footstep came back with its relatives.

Send a few dozen people running through here together, and the ears would have a very bad time.

en.html:
First time I saw Rokuhara's ruler with my own eyes, and that one word was the whole impression.

Strong, this man was.
In body. In mind. Every meaning you could give the word.

The breadth of his back alone spoke of how thickly the strength was laid on.

Goodness...
Righteousness, perhaps...
Neither one I could see.

Arrogant strength. Probably very simple desire was holding it up.

The urge to dominate, given a body?

But on that ground alone, unfit to rule Yamato I could not call him. Put one clean, upright, moral man at the top and the country arranges itself nicely—that much of a dreamer I was not.

A king full of ideals and short of power could make the country worse. East or west, open a history book and such fellows were available in quantity.

Moriuji Ashikaga was overflowing with power. The fate of all Yamato and every person in it—probably that back would not even find it heavy.

However greedy a tyrant he might be, if the Yamato held in those arms ended up protected...

Then as a ruler, was he right? Was he wrong?

Disliking the man was not supplying the answer.

ja.html:
六波羅総帥を初めて肉眼視しての感想は、ただその
一言に尽きた。

　この男は強いのだ。
　肉体的に。精神的に。<ruby>ありとあらゆる意味で<rt>・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　太い背が強さの厚みを物語っている。

　善性……
　あるいは義性といったものは、見受けられない。

　その強さは傲岸である。
　おそらく、ごくごく単純な<ruby>欲望<rt>・・</rt></ruby>に支えられているの
だろう。

　支配欲の権化か。

　しかし、それをもって彼に大和の統治者たるの資格
無しとは言えない。
　清く正しく道義に生きる者が上に立てば国は治まる
――と信じ込むほど俺も夢見がちではなかった。

　理想のみあって力足らぬ王は、むしろ国を乱す。
　東西の歴史を紐解けば、その種の前例は枚挙に暇が
ない。

　足利護氏は力に満ち溢れている。
　この背は大和全土全国民の命運も、重しとはしない
だろう。

　如何に彼が強欲極まる暴君であろうと――
　その両腕の抱え込む大和が、<ruby>結果的に<rt>・・・・</rt></ruby>守られるので
あれば。

　果たして彼は、統治者として是か、非か。

en.html:
Under Rokuhara, the people's burdens had certainly become much heavier than before. Suppressing the opposition, too, was done with an openness and severity beyond comparison.

But.
Therefore Rokuhara's rule was bad rule? Too much was being settled with that one therefore.

The circumstances had to be weighed also.

Six years ago, Rokuhara had committed an enormous betrayal. Sold the country, ended the war, and taken power in Yamato. Suppose it had not betrayed the country. Suppose it had fought the League's army on the home islands instead. What would have been left of the land? Scorched earth, no?

The Rokuhara shogunate was textbook militarism. Rights of the individual citizen, hardly worth considering. But remove that military system—was there no chance the continent's disorder would have spilled into Yamato?

These six years had hardly been an age of harmony for the world. Somehow or other, Rokuhara had got through them in peace. At least this much: no war against another country. Whether the previous system could have done the same, I did not know.

One hundred years later, some historian might call Rokuhara's rule “the best available method.”

ja.html:
六波羅体制下において、それ以前より、国民の負担
が大きく増しているのは確かな事実だ。
　反体制派に対する弾圧も、以前とは比較にならぬ程
露骨であり厳格である。

　が。
　よって六波羅の統治は悪政だ――と決め付けるのは
一概視が過ぎよう。

　情勢というものも併せて評価せねばならない。

　六年前、六波羅は途方もない裏切りを行い、国家を
売り、大戦に幕を引いた。そして大和の政権を得た。
　だがもし、六波羅が裏切らず、連盟軍と本土決戦を
繰り広げていたら？　国土は焦土と化さなかったか？

　六波羅幕府は手本のような軍国主義を敷いており、
国民一人一人の権利は全く軽視されている。
　だがこの軍国主義体制がなかったら？　大陸情勢の
混迷が大和にも波及する可能性はなかったろうか？

　世界的に見て調和の時代とは言い難いこの六年間を、
六波羅は曲がりなりにも平穏に――少なくとも他国と
交戦することだけはなく――乗り切っているのだ。
　過去の体制で同じことができたかはわからない。

　百年後の歴史家は、六波羅の統治を「最善の手法」
として評価するのかもしれなかった。

en.html: Many in present-day Yamato, seeing Rokuhara's tyranny with their own eyes, would probably feel the same as me. But from a later age, with the view made fully objective, surely that other judgment could be reached also. History could be quite comfortable with a conclusion we had to live inside. Sau saal baad, sab samajhdaar. A hundred years later, everybody wonderfully sensible. The beatings have stopped hurting by then; the people who received them are dead. Now pull up a chair and explain how necessary the whole arrangement was. From that chair, perhaps the explanation would even be correct. Kill Moriuji Ashikaga now. Put an end to the Rokuhara system—◆and who could promise that Yamato would not go straight to ruin?
en.text:

But from a later age, with the view made fully objective, surely that other judgment could be reached also. History could be quite comfortable with a conclusion we had to live inside.

Now pull up a chair and explain how necessary the whole arrangement was. From that chair, perhaps the explanation would even be correct.

Kill Moriuji Ashikaga now.
